uniform_one_sided_unit_barrier.statement: Let an orthodox regular S have a nonregular idempotent BAND E(S). No idempotent-separating homomorphism into a locally r-orthodox regular T can put the images of EVERY finite triple of E(S) under one common idempotent left unit, or under one common idempotent right unit. In particular there is no such globally/classwise one-sided-unital completion preserving the target local variety.
uniform_one_sided_unit_barrier.written_proof: Choose x,y,z in E(S) with u=xyxzx different from v=xyzx, both idempotents. If j(x),j(y),j(z) have a common idempotent right unit d, they all belong to the actual regular band D_d={a in E(T):ad=a}, by the proved principal-idempotent-band lemma. Its regular identity forces j(u)=j(v), contradicting idempotent separation. The left-unit proof is dual via B_d. Therefore even a finite-diagram monoidalization for all triples fails unless E(S) was already globally regular.
uniform_one_sided_unit_barrier.least_quotient_relevance: For any completely simple homomorphism of the source band E(S), its regular band image is completely simple and hence rectangular; consequently q(u)=q(v). Thus such a false completion would collapse a genuine SAME completely-simple-quotient fibre pair, including at the least quotient. It is the EXTRA common-unit completion that causes the collapse, not the actual canonical(M) relations.
